    {
      "id": "gap-1",
      "description": "Which evidence combinations actually establish or refute continuity of a concrete work matter across independent workplace messages, conversations, attachments, email, and Teams remains open.       "classification": "ACADEMIC",
      "priority": "HIGH",
      "status": "open",
      "suggested_search_query": "(\"work item identity\" OR \"work matter identity\" OR \"business event coreference\" OR \"cross-document event coreference\") AND (email OR \"workplace communication\" OR enterprise) AND (cross-thread OR cross-document OR cross-source)",
      "resolution_notes": "Still open after round 2. Papers 1906.01753, 2011.12249, doi-10-1038-s41598-025-32765-6, and doi-10-18653-v1-2023-emnlp-main-294 provide adjacent evidence about event arguments, participants, temporal/discourse context, structural links, or evidence combination, but they do not directly validate which combinations of workplace-specific signals establish or refute identity of a concrete work matter across independent messages, conversations, and attachments."
    },
    {
      "id": "gap-2",
      "description": "The application-specific decision policy remains open: the relative cost of false merges versus false splits, thresholds for attachment versus rejection, and exact semantics/calibration of CONTINUE, NEW, and UNCERTAIN must be determined from msgloom requirements and empirical evaluation. The reviewed literature supports rejection and risk-coverage trade-offs but does not establish msgloom's loss function or false-merge cost.",
      "classification": "ENGINEERING",
      "priority": "HIGH",
      "status": "open",
      "resolution_notes": "Resolve through product requirements and empirical benchmarking rather than additional literature search. Define operational semantics for CONTINUE, NEW, and UNCERTAIN; specify an explicit cost matrix for false merge, false split, incorrect continuation, and abstention; construct a representative labeled workplace validation set; sweep decision thresholds; measure precision, recall, merge/split error rates, calibration, and risk-coverage curves; then select thresholds and costs according to msgloom's accepted operational risk."
    },
    {
      "id": "gap-3",
      "description": "The msgloom correction and identity-state model remains open. Stable Topic IDs independent of generated labels or source thread IDs, versioned identity assessments, supersession links, immutable evidence lineage, and general MERGE/SPLIT correction require project-level design and testing. Incremental ER papers show that earlier clusters can be revised, but they do not define msgloom's identity/history semantics.",
      "classification": "ENGINEERING",
      "priority": "HIGH",
      "status": "open",
      "resolution_notes": "Resolve through architecture design, implementation prototypes, and invariant-driven tests. Define stable Topic identity independently from labels and source thread identifiers; model identity assessments as versioned records; preserve immutable evidence provenance; define supersession and correction semantics; specify deterministic MERGE and SPLIT operations and their effect on historical references; and test replay, idempotence, auditability, rollback, concurrent updates, and preservation of lineage. Papers 1402.4417 and doi-10-1007-978-3-030-49461-2-23 justify revisability of incremental clustering but do not determine these application semantics."
    },
    {
      "id": "gap-4",
      "description": "There is still no direct production-domain evidence in this corpus for longitudinal work-matter identity across Outlook email and Microsoft Teams. News, Wikipedia, image-recognition, public-health linkage, knowledge-graph, database-process, and general text results cannot establish production accuracy or representativeness for msgloom.",
      "classification": "ACADEMIC",
      "priority": "HIGH",
      "status": "open",
      "suggested_search_query": "(enterprise OR workplace OR organizational) AND (email OR \"Microsoft Teams\" OR \"enterprise chat\" OR \"workplace chat\") AND (cross-thread OR longitudinal OR cross-conversation) AND (\"topic identity\" OR \"task tracking\" OR \"case tracking\" OR \"event coreference\" OR \"conversation linking\")",
      "resolution_notes": "Still open after round 2. The reviewed studies, including 1906.01753, 2011.12249, 2104.05022, doi-10-18653-v1-2023-emnlp-main-294, and doi-10-1007-978-3-030-33223-5-12, do not evaluate longitudinal work-matter identity across Outlook email and Microsoft Teams or a sufficiently equivalent enterprise email/chat production corpus."
    },
    {
      "id": "gap-5",
      "description": "How partial, subevent, evolving, membership, or otherwise non-transitive relations should map onto workplace work-matter continuity remains unresolved. The corpus now provides stronger evidence that such relations exist and may be non-transitive, but no reviewed paper defines when those relations should mean CONTINUE, RELATED-BUT-SEPARATE, MERGE, SPLIT, or another workplace-specific relation.",
      "classification": "ACADEMIC",
      "priority": "HIGH",
      "status": "open",
      "suggested_search_query": "(\"partial event identity\" OR \"partial coreference\" OR \"subevent relation\" OR \"event evolution\" OR \"event membership\" OR \"non-transitive coreference\") AND (workflow OR task OR case OR workplace OR enterprise)",
      "resolution_notes": "Still open after round 2. The newly reviewed evidence identified by manual-35bac66e3c and manual-c43ffe3135 supports the existence of partial, subevent, membership, spatiotemporal-continuity, or non-transitive event relations, but it does not establish workplace-specific decision semantics mapping those relations to continuation, separation, merge, split, or another Topic relation."
    },
    {
      "id": "gap-6",
      "description": "The best operational strategy for Phase 2 evidence seeking remains unresolved. Retrieval-based event-coreference search and global-context models show that additional evidence can matter, but msgloom still needs engineering benchmarks for bounded historical retrieval, candidate generation, latency, retrieval stopping rules, and whether retrieved context actually changes identity decisions correctly.",
      "classification": "ENGINEERING",
      "priority": "MEDIUM",
      "status": "open",
      "resolution_notes": "Resolve with application-specific retrieval benchmarks. Implement competing candidate-generation and historical-retrieval strategies; vary time windows, candidate limits, lexical/semantic filters, conversation ancestry, artifact links, and stopping criteria; record retrieval recall, end-to-end latency, token/context cost, decision changes, correction rate, and false-merge/false-split effects. Compare no-retrieval, bounded retrieval, and progressively expanded retrieval on the same labeled stream. doi-10-18653-v1-2022-emnlp-main-58 and doi-10-18653-v1-2023-emnlp-main-294 motivate evidence seeking but do not determine msgloom's operational bounds."
    },
    {
      "id": "gap-7",
      "description": "Calibration under non-stationary workplace streams remains unresolved. Selective-classification guarantees assume representative calibration data, while cross-corpus event-coreference results demonstrate substantial distribution sensitivity; this corpus does not establish reliable calibration or abstention under workplace concept drift.",
      "classification": "ACADEMIC",
      "priority": "MEDIUM",
      "status": "open",
      "suggested_search_query": "(\"selective classification\" OR abstention OR \"confidence calibration\" OR \"selective prediction\") AND (\"distribution shift\" OR nonstationary OR streaming OR \"concept drift\") AND (text OR NLP OR coreference OR clustering)",

    }
